item.title: Client Side Dynamic Site on Github Pages
item.description:
GitHub Pages can host client-side dynamic applications (such as Single Page Applications built with React, Vue, or Angular) because it serves static files (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) that execute in the user’s browser.

However, it cannot host server-side rendered (SSR) applications or run backend code like PHP or Node.js directly.

Routing Challenges and Solutions

The 404 Issue

GitHub Pages does not support server-side routing (HTML5 pushState); refreshing a non-root route (e.g., /about) returns a 404 error because the server lacks a “front controller.”

item.title: Deploying this website
item.description:
This site is a static Hugo build with a custom theme, and getting it live came down to three pieces: a build pipeline, a host, and a domain.

The build pipeline

Rather than build locally and push the output, I added a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/hugo.yaml) that builds the site with Hugo on every push to main and deploys it to GitHub Pages. The Hugo version in the workflow is pinned to match what’s installed locally, so hugo server -D and CI never drift apart.

item.title: Hello, world
item.description:
This is the first post. Replace it with your own words — a good opener is why you’re writing in public and what a reader should expect.

A few things this theme handles out of the box:

  • Prose set in a readable serif at a comfortable measure.
  • Inline code and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting:
def teach(idea):
    return explain(idea, twice=True)

Blockquotes for the things other people said better.

That’s it. Write more posts with hugo new content posts/my-next-idea.md.
